newsitem.title: USA: Atlas Copco makes cash tender for Prime Service.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco makes cash tender for Prime Service.

text.p: Atlas Copco AB of Sweden said Monday it plans to buy machinery leasing company Prime Service Inc. in a $1.2 billion deal that is expected to accelerate consolidation in the U.S. equipment rental market.

Atlas Copco, an industrial engineering company, started a $32-a-share cash tender offer worth about $900 million and will assume $260 million debt in the friendly takeover, which was approved by board of Houston-based Prime Service, the companies said.

"One of the dimensions of growth is the consolidation of the industry, and you could say we will take part in that consolidation," Atlas Copco's Chief Executive Giulio Mazzalupi said in a conference call with analysts.
Prime Service's rental business also could boost sales for the Swedish firm's existing U.S. subsidiaries -- compressor makers Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp. and Chicago Pneumatic Tool Co., he said.
"Atlas Copco will also achieve a leading position in service of construction and industrial equipment in the U.S.," Mazzalupi said.

Prime Service ranks as the second-largest competitor in an $18 billion U.S. equipment rental market made up largely of "mom-and-pop" outlets and a handful of large corporations. Its 122 rental equipment locations in 14 states generated about $330 million in sales and operating profit of $66 million in 1996, Atlas Copco said.
Atlas Copco said the acquisition would boost cash flow per share but that earnings per share would decrease during the first two years by up to 5 percent.

"This acquisition should enable Atlas Copco to further expand its U.S. positions in construction and industrial equipment," said analyst Daniel Di Senso of Standard & Poor's, which may upgrade Prime Service's $66.7 million of debt securities and $298.5 million of bank debt.
Prime Service was acquired in December 1994 by Investcorp, certain international investors and Prime Service management. It was spun off in an initial public offering in October 1996.

"Investcorp and the other international investors, who currently own about 74 percent of the outstanding shares of Prime Service, have agreed to tender all of their shares as part of the Atlas Copco acquisition," the companies said.
The bid represents a 29 percent premium over Prime Service's $24.875 a share closing on June 6. The stock jumped $6.875 to $31.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
